title: Discover, Explain, Improve: An Automatic Slice Detection Benchmark for Natural Language Processing
findings: The paper's proposed slice detection model, Edisa, was shown to be effective at identifying error-prone data slices related to religious identity terms from the Jigsaw dataset. In experiments on the 'Jigsaw-religion' sub-dataset, Edisa consistently outperformed baseline methods in discovering mispredicted datapoints and was able to leverage these discovered slices to improve the base model's performance through techniques like selective prediction and prediction flipping.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured unintended model bias and systematic errors by evaluating model performance on data slices defined by religious identity terms. Specifically, it assessed a model's ability to automatically discover, explain, and improve performance on underperforming groups of datapoints related to religion in a toxicity detection task.
